title: Impact Intent Notes - Manager Priming
content:
Purpose: quick, candid primer for my manager 1:1 + my own running log for Q1->Q2 work priorities and evidence. Not a polished narrative — a pragmatic signal board so conversations are fast and decisions actionable.

Context (one-liner): I run people ops initiatives focused on frontline manager enablement, calibration tooling, and onboarding improvements. This quarter I’m leaning into two bets: (1) reduce new manager time-to-impact via a micro-fellowship and playbook, and (2) create light-weight calibration heuristics that scale to 150+ managers without heavy admin overhead.

Top outcomes I’m driving (owner-level outcomes — measurable):
- Reduce mean first-90-day ramp time for managers by 20% (baseline: avg 14 weeks -> target ~11 weeks).
- Pilot micro-fellowship with 8 manager participants and achieve NPS >= 8.0.
- Deliver calibration rubric + dashboard MVP that surfaces outlier teams (2x more likely to catch high-risk people decisions).
- Remove >30% of ad-hoc manager content requests by consolidating into self-serve playbook + 1-pagers.

Weekly priorities (this week):
- Finalize cohort cohort syllabus + calendar for micro-fellowship (deliverable: session guides + coach list).
- Pair with SRE data partner to validate calibration dashboard queries (meet Wed).
- Draft 1-pager on "first 30/60/90 for managers" for product managers and eng leads.

Signals I’m tracking (leading and lagging):
- Leading: number of manager sign-ups for micro-fellowship, playbook pageviews, time-to-first-action in onboarding checklist.
- Lagging: manager ramp time (HRIS + pulse surveys), NPS of fellowship, percent of escalations to People Ops for manager decisions.

Evidence (current snapshot):
- Pageviews to manager playbook beta: 180 unique views (since Feb 1) — decent but shallow engagement (avg time 1:12).
- 6 managers expressed interest in cohort; 2 tentative but need scheduling bandwidth.
- Baseline ramp time pulled from HRIS: median 14.1 weeks (N=24 managers onboarded last 12 months).
- Conversation log: two product leads asked for "simpler escalation flow" last week — shows demand.

Key hypotheses and risks (explicit):
1) Hypothesis: Short, cohort-based experiential learning will reduce ramp more than asynchronous docs because social accountability drives behavior. Risk: scheduling friction reduces participation and skews to already-high-performing managers.
2) Hypothesis: A compact calibration rubric (3 signals + 1 narrative) will be adopted because it reduces cognitive load. Risk: perk-itis — leaders will ask for more metrics and we re-create a heavy process.
3) Hypothesis: Consolidating ad-hoc content into 1-pagers will reduce requests. Risk: content discoverability — if we don't ship search/links in the right places, behavior won't change.

Manager conversation prompts (what I want to surface quickly):
- Which outcome do you want me to prioritize if I can do exactly one of the top outcomes this quarter? (expected answers: "ramp time" or "calibration")
- If we had to cut scope, remove which deliverable and why?
- Any blockers with leadership buy-in or capacity that I should escalate? (scheduling, partner bandwidth, budget)
- Feedback on proposed measurement approach: are these KPIs credible to you for performance conversations?

Requests for manager (ask list):
- Approve budget for cohort facilitator (est. $4k) by Mar 20.
- Introduce me to two senior PMs who can sponsor the pilot participants and champion time allocation.
- Quick read and reaction to the calibration rubric draft (I’ll send Friday).

Mini retro: what’s working / what to stop / experiments to try
- Working: rapid prototyping with one lead manager; quick alignment on use cases.
- Stop: long-form playbook edits — move to separate living doc and focus on short 1-pagers.
- Experiment: 2-hour kickoff + three 30-minute office hours vs. weekly 60-minute cohort session (test for participation vs. retention).

Concrete next actions (owned by me unless noted):
- Wed: meeting with SRE data partner to validate queries (Elena).
- Thu: draft fellowship syllabus + session outlines (Elena/Aisha).
- Fri: send calibration rubric v0 to manager for review (Elena).
- Mar 16: recruit first 8 participants (Elena + manager sponsors).

Notes to self (quick reminders):
- Keep artifacts minimal: 1-pagers, checklist, short sample scripts managers can copy.
- For measurement, prefer percent change vs absolute difference so we avoid tiny-n problems.
- Keep leader asks binary: approve / decline / defer with timeline.

Questions I still have (for manager / partner):
- Do we have budget flexibility to pay a fractional facilitator for the cohort?
- Can we leverage existing engineering "lunch-and-learn" slots to reduce scheduling friction?
- Who is the canonical owner for manager onboarding content in the docs stack (product docs vs people ops)?

Opening lines I might use in the 1:1 (two versions):
- Short: "Two asks today — budget approval for a pilot facilitator, and a quick read of a calibration rubric. Want to pick one as priority?"
- Context: "I’m piloting a micro-fellowship aimed at cutting manager ramp by ~20%; I have a small budget ask and want your read on the calibration rubric before I ship."

Archive / follow-up pattern: after each 1:1, move decisions to the action tracker and add a single-line summary in the playbook changelog (helps later audits).

Personal reflection (tone/energy): I’m excited about the fellowship framing because it’s tangible and coachable, but low on bandwidth. Need to guard against scope creep and keep close to early signals rather than perfect content.

If manager asks for a one-pager to share with execs: prepare a single slide with problem, pilot design, metrics, and ask (time + $). Keep it <150 words.

End of note.

Revision history (short):
- 2026-02-12: initial seed notes and hypotheses.
- 2026-02-26: added pageview data and cohort interest.
- 2026-03-10: updated weekly priorities and added explicit asks for manager.
